adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec at spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb ~line 121 uses xhr :put for remove_member, but routes.rb only defines a DELETE route, so the test will raise ActionController::RoutingError instead of asserting 422

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs template checks {{#unless automatic}} but `automatic` is a property of the group controller, not the member item view context, so the remove link renders even for automatic groups where the backend returns 422

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and the item view `group-member` uses `admin/templates/group_member` where it conditionally shows the remove link with `{{#unless automatic}}...{{/unless}}`. The item view/template context is per-member (and the view defines no `automatic` binding), so `automatic` is not guaranteed to resolve to the group’s `automatic` flag; if it resolves as undefined/falsey, the remove link will render even for automatic groups. Since `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` returns 422 for automatic groups, this creates broken UI behavior (showing an action that will fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group model removeMember sends user_id as body data on a DELETE request, which jQuery/proxies may drop, causing params.require(:user_id) to raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and removal to fail

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember` the client issues a `DELETE` to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` and supplies `data: { user_id: ... }` (no `user_id` in the URL). The server action `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `params.require(:user_id)`, so if the `user_id` payload is not parsed/forwarded for a DELETE (e.g., some stacks only reliably pass query params for DELETE), the action will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and member removal will fail. The controller spec uses `xhr :delete, ... user_id: ...` which more closely resembles query params and wouldn’t catch this client/server mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New spec test uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route requires delete, causing a routing error instead of asserting the 422 response

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the first `.remove_member` example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, while `config/routes.rb` wires `remove_member` to `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (and `put "members"` goes to `add_members`). This means the test doesn’t exercise the real HTTP method/route used in production (though in a controller spec it likely won’t raise a routing error because it invokes the action directly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages in group.js has an off-by-one error when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, showing an extra empty page and keeping 'next' clickable
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination edge case: when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, the logic allows navigating to an extra/empty last page (offset == total), resulting in no members shown and confusing UX (e.g., next remains possible).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec coverage for the rewritten public groups#members pagination endpoint (meta.total, offset, 50-record default, hidden group guard)

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially rewrites the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to always paginate and to return a new JSON shape with `members` plus `meta: { total, limit, offset }`, defaulting `limit` to 50 (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). The only specs changed/added in this PR are for `Admin::GroupsController` (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`); there is no corresponding controller spec added/updated for `GroupsController#members` to cover the new defaults, offset handling, or the new `meta` fields. The guardian visibility check in `find_group` remains but also has no spec coverage shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops nonexistent usernames with no error feedback to the admin, and the old spec expectation for this behavior was deleted without replacement

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the loop only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; otherwise the username is ignored and the action can still return `success_json` (no feedback about invalid/nonexistent usernames). The prior spec explicitly asserted this “silent success” behavior for nonexistent users (in the removed PATCH incremental tests: `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"`), and there is no replacement test covering the new `add_members` endpoint’s handling of nonexistent usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member relies on group.save after group.users.delete, and stale offset after removing the last member of the last page can show an empty trailing page; no test covers this

adjudication.rationale: The new pagination + membership removal flow can leave the UI on an empty trailing page. In `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, the requested `offset` is clamped using the *current* `user_count` (`var offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), which will be stale immediately after `removeMember` deletes a user. If you were on the last page (e.g. `offset=50, limit=50, user_count=51`) and remove the only user there, `findMembers()` will still request `offset=50` even though the new total is 50, so the server returns `members=[]` and `meta.total=50`. The controller computed `totalPages` (`Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`) also yields an extra page for exact multiples (50/50 => 2), so you can get stuck showing page 2/2 with no members. Additionally, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then checks `group.save`; since `delete` already persists the association change, a failed `save` would return an error even though the member was removed. The specs added for `.remove_member` don’t cover the last-page/offset behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropped capability and verification of group creation with initial members: new create action accepts only name/visible and no test covers the new create-then-add-members flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::GroupsController#create was changed to accept only top-level params (name, visible) and no longer supports setting initial members via usernames (previously params[:group][:usernames]/group.usernames). On the client side, admin-group.js now calls group.create() (no usernames) and membership is handled separately via Group#addMembers hitting PUT /admin/groups/:id/members.json. Specs cover .create (only name stripping) and .add_members independently, but there is no test asserting the new create-then-add-members flow (create a group, then add members) works together.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Input field is not cleared after addMembers succeeds, so a second click re-submits the same usernames (acknowledged TODO)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and includes a `// TODO: should clear the input`, but it never resets `usernames` afterward. Given `usernames` is bound to the `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` input in `group.hbs`, the field will retain the previous value and a second click will resubmit the same usernames. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/incompleteness issue but not necessarily a functional defect (server-side may be idempotent).

adjudication_records.issue_text: user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs and admin-group-selector.hbs contain unrelated whitespace-only reformatting that pollutes the review surface and blame history

adjudication.rationale: The cited changes are purely whitespace/indentation reformatting with no behavioral impact: `admin-group-selector.hbs` removes blank lines around `<input type="text">`, and `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` only adjusts indentation/newlines inside existing markup without changing elements, attributes, or bindings. This is a style/blame-history nit rather than a verifiable defect or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin_base.scss scope drift: shared .form-horizontal styles newly bound to .badges even though no badges code path is touched, so badge admin pages silently inherit new 350px input widths as a side effect

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly broadens the SCSS selector from being under `section.details .form-horizontal` to a new shared block `+.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... input, textarea, select { width: 350px; } ... } }` in `admin_base.scss`, while removing those width rules from the earlier `section.details` block. This means any admin page under a `.badges` container using `.form-horizontal` will now inherit the 350px input/textarea/select widths (and related label/margin rules) as a side effect, even though this PR otherwise appears focused on groups UI. That’s a real scope/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb: the admin 'users' route under admin groups is removed with no replacement consumer, migration note, or compatibility path, causing 404s for existing admin tooling or plugins

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior `get "users"` route under `admin/groups` in `config/routes.rb` and replaces it with `put "members"` and `delete "members"` (mapped to `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` / `#remove_member`). The frontend code in this PR is updated to use the new `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` endpoints for membership changes, and member listing is now fetched via `/groups/:name/members.json` (non-admin). However, the diff provides no compatibility alias/redirect for the removed `/admin/groups/:id/users` endpoint, so any external admin tooling/plugins depending on that route could indeed start 404ing. This is a backward-compatibility concern grounded in the route change, even though the core app has a replacement path for its own needs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create-with-members capability dropped rather than re-scoped: create() no longer accepts usernames, making a two-step save mandatory, and POST /admin/groups silently ignores usernames to create an empty group

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes creating a group with initial members in a single request: the JS model drops `createWithUsernames/saveWithUsernames` and `asJSON()` no longer includes `usernames` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js), and the server-side `Admin::GroupsController#create` now only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` (no `usernames`) (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb). Membership management is moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints (routes.rb + controller methods). So any client still sending usernames on POST /admin/groups would have them ignored, forcing a two-step create-then-add flow. This is a scope/backward-compatibility regression rather than an internal correctness defect, since the UI and specs were updated to match the new flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public /groups/:id/members response format changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} as an unversioned breaking change, causing external consumers to parse undefined for the member list

adjudication.rationale: The diff in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb changes the `members` action response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, which is an unversioned response-shape change for the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint. Internally the Ember templates were updated to iterate `members` instead of `model`, but nothing in the diff preserves backward compatibility for external consumers expecting an array at the top level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewritten spec drops coverage for silent-skip behaviors (adding non-existent users, removing non-members), leaving the new endpoints' tolerance of bogus input untested

adjudication.rationale: The old spec explicitly covered “succeeds silently” cases for bogus membership changes (adding non-existent users, removing non-members) under PATCH update. Those examples are removed, and the new endpoint specs only test happy paths (add two real users; remove an existing member) plus automatic-group 422s. The new implementations still have silent-skip behavior: `add_members` only adds when `User.find_by_username` returns a user (silently skipping unknown usernames), and `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` which is a no-op for non-members. That tolerance is untested after the rewrite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Membership changes are not transactional: add_members skips unknown usernames silently and reports blanket success_json even when zero users matched, so admins see a success toast with nothing changed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code splits `usernames` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, silently skipping unknown usernames. It then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if no usernames matched and no membership changed. This is diff-grounded (new `add_members` action) and could mislead the UI into showing success when nothing happened, but the diff doesn’t establish that this must be treated as an error, so it’s more a behavioral/UX/API-semantics concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query in add_members: User.find_by_username executed per username in a loop; should be a single User.where(username_lower: list)/IN lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds a loop `usernames.split(",").each` that calls `User.find_by_username(username)` for each entry, resulting in one DB query per username (N+1 style). This is a performance/scalability concern and could be improved with a single `User.where(...)` lookup, but it’s not a functional correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently succeeds on nonexistent usernames, returning success_json with no error reporting which usernames failed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is added only if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; nonexistent usernames are simply skipped with no error collection/reporting. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, regardless of whether any requested usernames were actually added (`usernames.split(",").each ... if user ... end` then `render json: success_json`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavior/UX/API feedback gap, but not necessarily a correctness defect since the code is explicitly written to ignore missing users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one pagination in totalPages: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page when user_count % limit == 0; should be Math.ceil
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the off-by-one error in totalPages caused by using Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, noting it creates an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit and suggesting Math.ceil instead. This matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unversioned API-contract break: PUT /admin/groups/:id no longer accepts group[usernames] and silently ignores nested payload, breaking old clients with 200 success; removed PATCH changes and GET users endpoints also break consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#update` to read top-level params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and removes handling of the previously accepted nested payload `params[:group]` including `group[:usernames]` (old `update_put`). As a result, clients still sending `group[usernames]` (or `group[...]` generally) will have those fields ignored, yet `group.save` can still succeed and return `success_json` (200), making this a backward-incompatible API contract change. The diff also removes PATCH-specific `update_patch` logic (previously processed `params[:changes]`) and replaces the admin group “users” route with `PUT/DELETE members`, which likewise breaks older consumers relying on those endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member renders success even when user_id was never a member; group.save is a no-op returning true, giving no feedback distinguishing removed from wasn't-there

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, regardless of whether the association actually existed. However, the previous implementation explicitly tested and allowed silent success when removing non-members (see removed spec: `it "succeeds silently when removing non-members"`). This suggests the “no feedback when wasn’t-there” behavior is intentional/unchanged, not a verifiable defect introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members.hbs template reads members from controller scope while findMembers sets members on the group model, breaking rendering unless controller is a proxying ObjectController

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` the loop was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, but `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.set("model", model)` (where `model` is the group) and only calls `model.findMembers();`. `findMembers` populates `members` on the *group model* (`self.setProperties({ members: ... })`) and the route does not set `controller.members`. Unless the group-members controller proxies model properties (e.g., is an `ObjectController`), `members` will be undefined and rendering will break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember/addMembers reload doesn't re-clamp offset against new page count, so removing a member while on the last page can land on a blank page

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember` and `#addMembers`, the success handler just calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset` (models/group.js: `removeMember`/`addMembers`). `findMembers` clamps the requested offset using the *current* `user_count` before the AJAX call: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`. If you remove the only member on the last page (e.g., total 51, limit 50, offset 50), `user_count` is still 51 when recomputing `offset`, so it stays 50 and the request goes out with `offset=50`. The server doesn’t clamp offset (groups_controller.rb `members` just does `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` and returns meta with the same offset), so it returns an empty `members` array for `total=50`, landing the UI on a blank page with `offset` still out of range. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded state transition: alias_level and visible remain writable on automatic groups with no restriction, widening mutability of system groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not widen mutability of automatic/system groups for `alias_level` or `visible`. In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, those fields are still set for all groups (including automatic), while only `name` changes are blocked for automatic groups (`group.name = ... if ... && !group.automatic`). The prior implementation (`update_put`) likewise allowed `alias_level` and `visible` to be updated even when `group.automatic` (it only ignored/prohibited rename and membership changes). The new spec even asserts changing `visible` on an automatic group succeeds, indicating this is intentional behavior, not an unguarded transition newly introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route param mismatch: member routes under resources :groups populate params[:id], but add_members and remove_member call params.require(:group_id), raising ActionController::ParameterMissing on every real request, breaking member add/remove in production
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the routes under `resources :groups` supply the group identifier as `params[:id]`, but the controller/actions incorrectly read/require `params[:group_id]`, causing missing-parameter failures and breaking group membership access/modification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Specs exercise remove_member via :put but the route is defined as delete; Rails functional tests bypass routing so they cannot catch the verb/param mismatch, creating false confidence

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines the admin route for removing a member as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (config/routes.rb), and the client uses `type: "DELETE"` (group.js `removeMember`). But the controller spec exercises `remove_member` with `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` in the “cannot remove members…” example. Since controller specs invoke the action directly (not via route recognition), this test won’t catch an HTTP verb mismatch and could pass even if the route/client contract were wrong. This is a test correctness gap, not a runtime bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create-with-membership workflow was removed without replacement: create no longer accepts usernames, forcing a two-step process, and old tests asserting create with usernames were deleted rather than adapted

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the one-step “create group with members” flow: the Ember model deletes `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames` and `asJSON` no longer includes `usernames` (now only `{name, alias_level, visible}`), and `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` with no usernames handling. Membership changes are moved to separate endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`) and the UI only shows member management when `{{#if id}}` (after creation). The spec coverage that asserted create with usernames was deleted rather than adapted to the new two-step workflow, which is a concrete review concern but not a verifiable correctness bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Add-members flow leaves entered usernames in the selector after a successful add (per the author's own TODO), causing re-submission of same usernames on subsequent clicks with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and, after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));`, it never resets `usernames` to empty/null. Since the `user-selector` in `group.hbs` is bound to `usernames=usernames`, the entered usernames will remain in the selector after a successful add, enabling accidental re-submission on subsequent clicks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members route's setupController no longer returns the findMembers() promise, so rendering races the AJAX call, risking blank/flash-of-empty members lists and silently swallowed errors
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: findMembers() became asynchronous and its promise is not returned/handled in the controller, leading to a race where the UI may render before member data is available (and errors may be swallowed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset parameters in groups_controller.rb members action allow any authenticated user to request the entire membership list in one query, enabling DoS and bulk user-enumeration on large automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are taken directly from request params and passed into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper-bound or sanity checks. A caller who can access the group (via `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`) can supply an arbitrarily large `limit` (and potentially negative/huge `offset`), causing very large queries/responses and enabling bulk member enumeration / potential DoS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently skips non-existent usernames and still returns success, causing a fail-open authorization workflow where admins believe access was granted but it wasn't

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, otherwise it does nothing and still returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if no members were added). So the “silently skips non-existent usernames and still returns success” part is accurate. However, calling this a “fail-open authorization workflow” is not supported by the diff: only admins can hit this controller, and the previous implementation explicitly had a spec asserting silent success when adding non-existent users, suggesting this behavior may be intentional rather than a newly introduced defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing happy-path test for update on a non-automatic group: deleted test 'is able to update group members' was not replaced, leaving alias_level/visible/name changes uncovered, including the !group.automatic rename branch tested only negatively

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update to accept top-level params (alias_level/visible/name) and introduces an automatic-group rename guard (`group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic`). In the controller spec, the previous non-automatic happy-path update test (updating members and name) is removed and not replaced; the remaining `.update` coverage only asserts the negative case for automatic groups (name not changed, visible updated). There is no test asserting that a non-automatic group can successfully update name/alias_level/visible under the new parameter contract, leaving that branch/behavior unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members tests do not cover silently skipping unknown usernames (deleted tests 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' and 'can make incremental adds' not replaced), and the automatic-group 422 test doesn't verify no membership was created

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the old PATCH-based incremental membership update tests (including “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”) with new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoint tests, but the new spec only tests adding two valid users and the 422 on automatic groups (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, contexts ".add_members" / ".remove_member"). Meanwhile the new implementation in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` explicitly skips unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` (no else/error), so the previously-covered behavior still exists but is no longer tested. Also, the automatic-group 422 test asserts only status and does not assert that membership was unchanged (it calls `group_id: 1` and never checks member count), so it doesn’t verify the side effect didn’t occur. This is a concrete coverage gap for new/changed logic, not a demonstrable runtime bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action's error branch (render_json_error on failed save, e.g. duplicate/invalid name) has no test triggering it; only the success path is covered, and the failure response shape is never verified

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, the new failure path `else render_json_error group` is reachable (e.g., invalid/duplicate name), but the updated specs under `context ".create"` only exercise the success case (`xhr :post, :create, name: " bob "` expecting 200 and a created group). There is no test that forces `group.save` to fail and verifies the error response/status/shape from `render_json_error`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Groups controller members endpoint's new meta {total, limit, offset} response contract and pagination handling has no spec, and the removed automatic-group pagination branch is a behavior change with zero assertions

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate (default `limit = 50`, `offset = params[:offset].to_i`) and to return a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), removing the prior behavior that only applied `limit/offset` for automatic groups and otherwise returned a plain serialized array. The PR adds/updates specs only for `Admin::GroupsController` (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb) and includes no spec coverage for `GroupsController#members`’ new response contract or the behavior change from unpaginated/non-meta to paginated/meta.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action in admin/groups_controller.rb silently drops membership payload (e.g. group[usernames]) that old clients send, so membership changes are acknowledged but never written to group_users

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update the diff switches from reading membership changes via `payload = params[:group]` / `group.usernames = payload[:usernames]` to only handling top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]`. There is no handling of `params[:group][:usernames]` anymore, so an old client sending `group[usernames]` will have that payload ignored while `group.save` can still succeed and return `success_json`, resulting in acknowledged-but-not-applied membership changes. Membership updates were moved to separate `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints, but the update action itself is now silently non-backwards-compatible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action in admin/groups_controller.rb no longer applies params[:group][:usernames], so groups created via the old payload get zero members silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Admin::GroupsController#create` to read top-level `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` and no longer applies `params[:group][:usernames]` (previously used to seed members on create). That is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/API change. However, the finding’s claim that the “old payload” will create groups with zero members *silently* is not strictly verifiable: if a client sends only the old nested payload (`group[name]`, `group[usernames]`), `params[:name]` will be nil and `group.name` becomes "", likely causing validation failure rather than creating an empty-members group. Still, backwards compatibility for clients that previously relied on `usernames` at create is a concrete concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint in groups_controller.rb unconditionally applies a default limit of 50, silently truncating member lists for callers that don't pass limit (old endpoint returned full list)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes behavior from returning the full ordered member list for non-automatic groups to always applying pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. Previously, only `automatic?` groups were limited/offset (default 200), otherwise all members were rendered. This means callers that omit `limit` will now only receive the first 50 members, i.e., silent truncation compared to the old behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint response shape changed from a bare array to {members:, meta:}, breaking old parsers

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array of members) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total:, limit:, offset: } }` (an object wrapper). This is a backward-incompatible API change for any existing clients expecting an array from `/groups/:group_id/members`, so the finding that old parsers would break is supported by the diff.
